description: A Cineris configuration file: the user's `config.toml`, a project's `.cineris/config.toml` or `.cineris/config.local.toml`, or the managed file. Generated from the settings in `crates/cineris-config`; not edited by hand. `x-cineris-trust` says what a project's file may set, and `x-cineris-effect` when a change takes effect.

effort.description: The reasoning level the model runs at unless a role sets its own: one of its levels, or an alias. `model.effort` and a role's `effort` win over it.

prompt_style.description: The prompt style: `concise`, or `guided` for more guidance on the tools.

tool_schema.description: How tools are declared: `strict` (the provider checks the arguments, where the model can) or `loose` (the harness alone).

variants.description: Variant overrides by model: `[adapt.variants."claude-opus-5-5"]` with `edit_format`, `tool_schema`, `prompt_style` or `effort`. An override wins over the catalog's default for that model, and applies from the next context epoch that builds a prompt. A choice the build does not know stops the session from starting, with the choices it has. The user's alone.

compat.description: Which files written for other tools are read.

instructions.description: Instruction files under the names other tools use, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, in the workspace. Off, only the names in `context.instruction_names` are read there; the user's own files in the configuration directory are read either way.

mcp.description: MCP server definitions of other clients, offered for import.

config_version.description: The version of the configuration schema the file was written for. A file with a newer version than this build understands is refused.

context.description: When the conversation is compacted, and which instruction files are read.

auto_compact.description: Whether the conversation is compacted by itself when a request would pass `compact_at`, or the provider says a request does not fit. Off, the turn stops there and asks for a compaction (`session/compact`) or a new session.

background.description: Whether a summary is prepared in the background from `prepare_at`, on the `fast` role's model (the main model when there is none), so that the compaction need not wait for it. The user's alone: off, every compaction waits at the trigger for its summary, and a repository's file must not make the sessions in it wait.

compact_at.description: The trigger: the fraction of what a request may hold (the model's context window less room for the answer and a margin) past which the conversation is compacted before the request. Never below what a compaction needs, the prompt and the tools and room for a summary: a lower value is raised to that, and the user is told. From a project, after trust: a compaction costs a request.

instruction_names.description: More names of instruction files, read after `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in each directory. From a project, after trust: what they hold is sent with every request.

instructions_cap.description: The most the instruction files may hold in all, in bytes. Past it the innermost files are cut, and the user is warned. From a project, after trust.

keep_recent_tokens.description: How much of the most recent conversation a compaction replays after its summary, without its reasoning, in tokens. 0 replays nothing. At most half of what the trigger leaves once the prompt and the tools are counted, and the user is told when that holds it back. From a project, after trust.

prepare_at.description: The fraction past which a summary is prepared in the background. From a project, after trust.

credentials.description: Where stored credentials are kept. Never the credentials themselves: no key of this file is meant for a key, and a provider's literal header, which may hold one, is redacted.

store.description: The store for API keys saved with `cineris auth login`.

enabled.description: Whether the user's own extension of this name is loaded. `false` keeps it out of every new session, its tools, commands and prompt with it; its pin is kept, so `true` again needs no new approval unless its folder changed. A project's extension of the name is not turned off by it: a project's is kept out by not trusting the project.

extensions.description: Extensions by name: `[extensions.<name>]`, which only turns one off (`cineris ext disable` writes it). The user's alone: a project's entry is ignored, since a project's extension is kept out by not trusting the project, and a project may not turn the user's own off.

http.description: The HTTP client: the connect timeout, a proxy, and extra certificate authorities.

index.description: The repository map: whether epochs are given one, its budget, and the caps of the index it is made from.

map.description: Whether each context epoch is given the repository map: the workspace's directories and its most relevant files with their main definitions. The `outline` tool works either way.

map_tokens.description: The map's budget, in tokens. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: the map is sent with every request of an epoch.
map_tokens.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

map_wait.description: How long the first request of an epoch waits for the map when it is not ready yet; past it, the map follows as a notice at the next boundary where it is. Unset, 150 ms in the interactive app and none in a headless run, whose start it would otherwise slow. At most one second. The user's alone: the wait is paid by every epoch's first request, and a repository's file must not make the sessions in it wait (found by the independent review of step 18).

max_file_bytes.description: The largest file the index reads, in bytes. A larger one is listed and not outlined, unless the `outline` tool is asked for it.
max_file_bytes.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

max_files.description: The most files the index reads. Past it, the files nearest the top of the tree are indexed, and the map says it is partial.
max_files.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

pass_time.description: The most time one pass of the index spends reading files, after its listing (which its cap on entries bounds). One that runs out carries on when the session is next idle. At least 250 ms is used, whatever is set: less would make an idle session pass over the workspace again for every few files.
pass_time.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

keys.description: The terminal UI's key bindings, by the context an action belongs to: `[keys] editor.new_line = ["shift+enter", "ctrl+j"]`.

dialog.description: A dialog's: the answers to an approval, a question or trust.

editor.description: The editor's actions: `submit`, `new_line`, `undo`, and the rest.

focus.description: A focused tool box's or panel's.

fork.description: The fork of the pickers that fork (`/rewind`'s, `/sessions`'): `fork`.

global.description: Those looked up last, whatever has the keyboard: `interrupt`, `redraw`, `suspend`, and the rest.

screen.description: The full-screen presenter's: scrolling, searching, and the mouse's `click`, `wheel_up` and `wheel_down`.

viewer.description: The viewer's (`Ctrl+O`): moving between boxes, opening one, scrolling, searching, and the mouse's `click`, `wheel_up` and `wheel_down`.

limits.description: The most a turn, a session and a day may spend.

day.description: Limits on one local day, across every session of every process on this machine, counted from the statistics: with `stats.enabled = false` a session with a day's limit is refused when it opens. Another process's requests are counted once they end, so the ones in flight when the limit is reached can pass it (`docs/architecture/18-usage.md`, "Limits on one day").

cost.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

requests.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

time.description: Wall-clock time. Held for a turn and a session; a day's is accepted and not held yet (`docs/outstanding/a-days-time-limit.md`).
time.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

tokens.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

cost.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

requests.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

time.description: Wall-clock time. Held for a turn and a session; a day's is accepted and not held yet (`docs/outstanding/a-days-time-limit.md`).
time.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

tokens.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

cost.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

requests.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

time.description: Wall-clock time. Held for a turn and a session; a day's is accepted and not held yet (`docs/outstanding/a-days-time-limit.md`).
time.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

tokens.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

level.description: The level (`error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`), optionally followed by levels for target prefixes: `"info,cineris_llm=debug"`. The `CINERIS_LOG` variable and `--log-level` override it.

managed.description: For the managed file of a shared machine only.

locked.description: Keys that no layer above the managed file may change. A table's name locks every key in it. Read from the managed file only.

mcp.description: MCP servers by name, and MCP settings.

model.description: Models by role, the reasoning level and the speed tier.

effort.description: The reasoning level of the main role: one of the model's own levels, or `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max`. From a project, after trust: more reasoning is more output.

fast.description: The model for utility calls: summaries, titles. Without one, the main model is used. From a project, after trust.

judge.description: The model for model-graded comparisons. Without one, the main model is used. From a project, after trust.

main.description: The model for the agent's own turns. Needed to run a turn. A project's file may choose one once the project is trusted: a model can cost more than the user's.

max_output.description: The most output tokens one response may have. Without it, the model's own limit applies. From a project, after trust.

reasoning.description: How much of the model's reasoning is shown.

effort.description: The role's reasoning level. For `main` it overrides `model.effort`. From a project, after trust.

provider.description: The provider that serves the role's model. Needed only when two providers have a model with the same name. From a project, after trust: it chooses the model as much as the name does.

speed.description: The role's speed tier. For `main` it overrides `model.speed`. From a project's file, a tier other than `standard` waits for trust.
speed.x-cineris-trust: by value: `standard` is a preference, any other tier raises cost

speed.description: The session's speed tier, which the main role runs at: `standard`, `fast` where the model offers it, or a provider's own tier name. The utility roles do not follow it: they run at `standard` unless `model.roles.<role>.speed` says otherwise. A project's file may set `standard`; any other tier costs more, and waits for the user to trust the project.
speed.x-cineris-trust: by value: `standard` is a preference, any other tier raises cost

speed_cooldown.description: How long requests stay at `standard` after a fallback, when the provider does not say when the tier is available again. From one minute, the window a provider counts its limits in, so that a session does not change speed (and perhaps write its cache again) every few requests; to an hour, past which a tier that keeps refusing is better turned off with `model.speed`.

speed_cooldown_min.description: The least time requests stay at `standard` after a fallback when the provider does say when the tier is available again: its time, or this long, whichever is later. `"0s"` takes the provider's time as given. At most an hour, as `speed_cooldown` is.

speed_fallback.description: Whether a request that a speed tier refuses is sent again at `standard`. When off, such a refusal is an ordinary rate limit.

speed_wait.description: The longest one request waits in place for a speed tier before it falls back to `standard`. `"0s"` never waits. At most two minutes: past that, `standard` answers sooner than the tier would, whatever keeping it saves. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: every wait is the session's.
speed_wait.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

models.description: Catalog overrides and additions: limits, prices, reasoning control, capability flags. Each `[models.<name>]` table is one whole catalog entry, with the keys of a `[[model]]` table of the built-in catalog, and replaces the built-in entry for the same provider and model. The entries are read by the model catalog itself when the program starts, which refuses one it does not understand: nothing is started then, and the error names the file, the entry and what is wrong.

permissions.description: The permission mode and the permission rules.

mode.description: The session's level: how much runs without asking.
mode.x-cineris-trust: by level: not above the mode in effect is a preference, up to `supervised` widens access, above it user only

rules.description: Permission rules. Every layer adds to the list; `deny` beats `ask` beats `allow`, whatever the order.
rules.x-cineris-trust: by action: `deny` and `ask` are preferences, `allow` widens access

profile.description: The profile to apply: the name of a `[profiles.<name>]` table. The `--profile` flag overrides it. A project's file may define profiles and may not select one: a profile the user wrote is applied with the user's rights, so a repository that could pick it could switch on whatever the user's loosest profile allows.

profiles.description: Named sets of settings. A profile may hold any key of this file except `profile`, `profiles`, `managed` and `config_version`.

project.description: The project profile and memory: whether commands are learned, and the budget of the profile's section of the prompt.

learn.description: Whether the harness learns from the commands a session runs: a build, test or check command that succeeds twice becomes an entry of the project profile, and a test command seen to fail and then pass with nothing changed a flaky one. Off, nothing is observed; what is already known is used as before, and `remember` and the user's own entries work. The user's alone: a repository's file does not decide what is kept about it.

profile_tokens.description: The budget of the project profile's section of the system prompt, in tokens, counted at three bytes a token. Entries past it are left out, commands last, and the section says how many. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: the section is sent with every request.
profile_tokens.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

capabilities.description: Capability flags of the endpoint, as the provider's protocol names them. For `anthropic-messages`: `replay_reasoning` (`"all"` for a server that leaves out the reasoning a model cannot read, as Anthropic's own does), `eager_tool_streaming`, `api_version` and `beta`. Each value is text, a whole number or `true`/`false`.

enabled.description: Whether the provider is available. `false` removes an entry that a lower layer or the built-in table defines.

first_event_timeout.description: How long to wait for the first event of a response. Overrides `retry.first_event_timeout` for this provider, within the same range: 30 seconds to an hour.

headers.description: Extra headers for every request. A value is text, or `{ env = "NAME" }` to read an environment variable when used. Text may be a key (some gateways take one in a header), so it is held as a secret and `cineris config show` prints it as `[redacted]`; a variable's name is shown.

idle_timeout.description: How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. Overrides `retry.idle_timeout` for this provider, within the same range: 30 seconds to an hour.

key_env.description: The environment variable that holds the provider's API key. It is looked at before the credential store. A built-in provider that takes a key has one already (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and so on). A provider with a key variable and no key anywhere is refused before anything is sent. One with none, as the built-in local servers have none, is asked without a key unless one is stored for it.

protocol.description: The wire protocol the endpoint speaks.

providers.description: Providers by name. A built-in provider needs no entry; an entry changes it or adds a new one. `enabled = false` removes one.

retry.description: How a request that failed is tried again.

attempts.description: The most attempts for one request, the first included. From a project, after trust: each attempt can be paid for.

backoff_base.description: The wait before the second attempt. Each later wait is this multiplied by `backoff_factor` again, up to `backoff_cap`. From 100 ms, below which the attempts are spent before a brief outage can pass, to a minute. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
backoff_base.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

backoff_cap.description: The longest wait between two attempts. From a second, so that the attempts span more than a moment, to five minutes, past which a provider is down rather than busy. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
backoff_cap.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

backoff_factor.description: What the wait is multiplied by after each attempt. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it: a larger one makes every later wait longer.
backoff_factor.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

first_event_timeout.description: How long to wait for the first event of a response. From 30 seconds, below which a long prompt would fail every time, to an hour, past the ten minutes the built-in entries give a local server. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
first_event_timeout.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

idle_timeout.description: How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. From 30 seconds, within which a hosted provider that is still working sends a token or a ping, to an hour, past the five minutes the built-in entries give a local server. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
idle_timeout.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

max_wait.description: The longest wait a provider may ask for. A longer one ends the turn with the error and the provider's hint. From a minute, the window a provider counts its limits in, so that no file can make an ordinary rate limit end a turn, to an hour, past which the wait is a quota and not a rate limit. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
max_wait.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

rpc.description: The RPC server (`cineris serve`): how long it waits for its clients.

approval_timeout.description: How long an approval waits for a client's answer before it is a denial (`"0s"`: for as long as it takes). The terminal UI is not a server and sets none.

stalled_client.description: How long a client may take nothing the server sends while whole events wait for it past its queue, before its connection is closed. The session goes on.

runs.description: The run engine: concurrency, workspaces, budgets.

sandbox.description: What a command the harness starts may touch.

enabled.description: Whether commands are confined by the OS sandbox where there is one.

network.description: Whether a command may use the network. `off`: no TCP or UDP, to this machine's own addresses included, and no Unix socket, so a test suite that starts a server on loopback or on a Unix socket fails in the sandbox; such a run needs `full`, or one approved run outside the sandbox. `full`: the network (TCP and UDP, loopback included), and nothing else: still no Unix socket (the session bus, an agent, the Docker socket), no virtual machine's socket to its host, no raw socket.
network.x-cineris-trust: by value: `off` is a preference, `full` widens access

protect.description: Paths a command may not change, besides the built-in ones. Every layer adds to the list.

write.description: Paths a command may write besides the workspace. Every layer adds to the list.

data_dir.description: The data directory. A leading `~` is the home directory. Without it the platform's usual place is used.

durability.description: When the session log is flushed to the disk: after every item (`item`), at the end of every turn (`turn`), or never, leaving it to the operating system (`never`). The user's alone: a project that could choose `never` could cost the user their sessions. A session already open keeps what it was opened with.

shell.description: The shell that runs commands, the time a command may take, and the environment variables it is not given.

args.description: The arguments before the command, in place of the shell's own: `["-l", "-c"]` for a login bash. The command is always passed after them, last.

env_remove.description: Environment variables that commands are not given, besides the key variables of the providers, which are always removed. A name may end with `*` for every variable that starts so. Every layer adds to the list. A project's entries wait for trust: `"*"` would take `PATH` away and stop every command.

max_timeout.description: The longest time limit a command may ask for. From ten seconds, below which a build or a test run could never finish, to a day. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
max_timeout.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

program.description: The shell: a program's name on `PATH`, or its path. How it is spoken to follows its name: `bash`, `pwsh`, `powershell` and `cmd` each by their own rules, and any other as a POSIX shell. Unset, it is bash and then sh on Linux, and on Windows PowerShell 7, then Windows PowerShell, then cmd.exe. A project's file may not choose the program that runs every command.

timeout.description: The time limit of a command that asks for none, held to `max_timeout`. From a second, below which every command would fail, to half an hour, past which a command that hangs holds up its turn too long. A project's file may lower it and may not raise it.
timeout.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

stats.description: Whether local statistics are recorded, and for how long.

enabled.description: Whether events are recorded. Off, nothing is written, every adaptive feature uses its default, and the usage view has the open session's figures alone.

retention.description: How many months a monthly file of events stays after its own month: 3 by default. What it added up to stays in the aggregates, every all-time figure with it, so only the raw events go (a heavy user's are about 90 MB a month). Read each time the files are pruned, so a reload changes it at once.

terminal.description: What the terminal can do, in place of detecting it. Each is detected when it is not set.

backspace.description: What byte 0x08 is: `ctrl+h` reads it as Backspace, for a terminal whose Backspace sends `^H`; `del` as `Ctrl+Backspace`, which most terminals send it for; `auto` decides from the terminal's erase character.

bracketed_paste.description: Bracketed paste: `true` trusts the terminal's brackets; `false` does not ask for them, and takes keys that come many at once with a line break inside for a paste; unset, it asks, and takes such a burst for a paste only where the terminal has not said it knows the mode.

clipboard.description: Whether the terminal takes the clipboard sequence `/copy` sends: `false` also shows the text in the viewer, to select and copy by hand. Unset, it is guessed from the terminal: not the old console host, tmux or GNU screen.

keyboard.description: The enhanced keyboard protocol, which tells `Shift+Enter` from `Enter`.

mouse.description: The mouse in the viewer and the full-screen presenter: a click opens or closes a box, and the wheel scrolls; `shift` and a drag still select text. Never in the inline screen. On unless set to `false`.

paste_wait.description: How long a bracketed paste may pause before what it holds is given as a paste; what follows of it, to its end, is its rest.

sync.description: Synchronized updates: each frame shown at once.

tools.description: Enabled tools, output limits and per-tool settings.

tui.description: The terminal UI: how the transcript is drawn.

density.description: A blank line between blocks (`comfortable`), or only between turns (`compact`).

glyphs.description: The glyph set: `auto` (Unicode where the terminal can show it), `unicode` or `ascii`. `ascii` suits a terminal that draws the box's edges and the marks of East Asian ambiguous width wide.

presenter.description: How the interface draws: `inline` (the transcript in the terminal's own scrollback) or `fullscreen` (the whole window, on the alternate screen, scrolled and searched there). `--fullscreen` chooses the second for one run.

prose_width.description: The widest prose may be, in columns, its indent included. The window's width when that is less.

reasoning.description: What finished reasoning leaves in the transcript: its `summary`, or only how long it took (`duration`).

reduced_motion.description: A still mark in place of the spinner.

theme.description: The theme: `auto` (dark or light, from the terminal's background), `dark` or `light`. A name the interface does not know is said, and `auto` is used.

tool_detail.description: The most diff lines a tool's box opens on by itself, and the most rows of detail an open box shows while its round runs.

tool_output.description: Which tool detail starts open: `auto` (a failure's output and a diff of up to `tool_detail` lines), `always` or `never`.

turn_summary.description: A dim line after each turn with its time, tokens and cost.

usage.description: The usage view: week start, ranges and the opt-in refresh.

ranges.description: `calendar` weeks and months, or `rolling`: the last 7 and 30 days.

refresh.description: The providers whose documented usage endpoint `cineris usage --refresh` may ask, with that provider's own key: `["openrouter"]`. Empty, nothing is ever asked. Only when the user asks, never on its own. The user's alone: a project's file cannot turn it on.

week_start.description: The first day of a week: `monday` to `sunday`.

verify.description: The project's checks at the end of a turn: whether they run, the user's own commands, the rounds and the time limits.

commands.description: The user's own checks, each a command line run in the workspace root, before the accepted test and check commands of the project profile. Every one of the user's layers adds to the list. The user's alone: a repository proposes its checks as command entries of `.cineris/profile.toml`, which each user accepts.

mode.description: `auto`: the checks run, and a failure goes back to the model. `ask`: they are offered, and run when the user asks. `off`: they run only when the user asks. A project's file may turn it down, and may not turn it up.
mode.x-cineris-trust: lower only: at or below the mode in effect (`off` < `ask` < `auto`) is a preference, a higher one is user only

round_time.description: The time one round's checks may take together. From ten seconds to an hour. A project's file may lower it.
round_time.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

rounds.description: The most rounds of checks one turn gets: a failure is given to the model, and the checks run again when it has changed files, until this many have run. A project's file may lower it.
rounds.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

turn_time.description: The time one turn's checks may take, every round together. From ten seconds to four hours. A project's file may lower it.
turn_time.x-cineris-trust: tighten only: a lower limit is a preference, a first limit where there was none waits for trust, a higher one is user only

title: Cineris configuration
